A NOTE ON ATTENTION / AN ORIGINAL ESSAY

The space
between things.

An editorial exercise · 1 min read · Fictional portfolio

Not every part of a page needs to speak at once. A title can set the direction, a paragraph can carry the thought, and a little space can give the reader time to arrive.

We often treat space as the absence of something. In an interface, it can be a kind of explanation. It tells us what belongs together, what deserves attention, and where one idea makes room for another.

The same is true of a working day. Leave enough room to ask a better question. Make the smallest useful thing. Then give someone else a chance to tell you what they see.

Clarity is not the result of removing everything. It is the result of understanding which things are doing a useful job, and letting those things breathe.

END OF ESSAY / SMALL THINGS, CONSIDERED
